promptLatex: Two fair coins are flipped. What is the probability that at least one of them shows heads?
hintLatex: "At least one" asks for two different cases, so look at the other event instead.
The complement is that both coins show tails, which is a single outcome.
That has probability $\frac{1}{4}$, so the answer is $1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$.
solutionLatex:
Two flips of a fair coin give $4$ equally likely outcomes.

The event "at least one head" is the complement of "both tails", which is the single outcome $(T,T)$. So $P(\text{both tails}) = \frac{1}{4}$.

Therefore $P(\text{at least one head}) = 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$.
